A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, including their figures, equations and appendices. They describe the same CRAFT-based psychophysics research, with matching procedures and retained experiments despite substantial revisions and a new title.

before.justification: V1 reports three original human psychophysics experiments, feature-occlusion results and supplementary selection-sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original behavioral results for ResNet50 and VGG16, together with gradient-based importance and dictionary axis-alignment analyses.

M1.justification: The core representation-construction algorithm remains CRAFT/NMF applied to activations from 300 maximally activating images, learning ten dictionary elements and selecting the most frequently maximally activated element. Renaming representations, evaluating VGG16 and changing diagnostic metrics do not alter this extraction procedure.

E1.justification: V1's Experiment III tests mixed natural images and MACO-generated visualizations; this distinct stimulus scenario is removed. V2's Experiment III instead applies the retained natural-image, semantically controlled task to VGG16. ImageNet and the participant population remain unchanged; VGG16 itself is a model comparison, not a new dataset.

E2.justification: V2 adds VGG16 as an explicitly evaluated comparator to ResNet50, creating a central architecture comparison under both representational bases in Section 4.3. V1 evaluates only ResNet50. The within-model comparison between individual neurons and CRAFT-derived dictionary elements is retained.

E3.justification: V2 replaces feature-occlusion logit drops with Gradient×Input importance and introduces axis-alignment measurement. It adds VGG16 evaluation using 80 neurons across 11 ReLU layers. Reported analyzed samples for Experiments I/II change from 138/133 to 133/130, alongside a reported three-standard-deviation completion-time exclusion. Semantic matching is described using nine rather than ten images; the PDFs do not establish whether stimuli were regenerated.

E4.justification: V2 removes the quantitative semantic-control analyses, their trial-distribution figure, the mixed-image visualization study and Appendix C's comparison of element selection using 300 versus 2,900 images. It adds cross-model axis-alignment analysis and revises the depth analysis. Its new appendix discusses selection alternatives conceptually, without replacing the removed empirical sensitivity test.

E5.justification: V1 specifies trial-level logistic mixed-effects models with participant and unit random effects. V2 replaces these behavioral analyses with Mann–Whitney tests and depth correlations, introduces Bonferroni correction, and uses one-sample t-tests of paired importance differences. Both versions report 95% confidence intervals; the substantive change concerns statistical procedures rather than merely different estimates.

E6.justification: Experiments I/II retain their reported mean accuracies, although significance statistics change. V1's mixed-stimulus Experiment III reports 80.0% versus 74.1%; v2's different VGG16 experiment reports 81.5% versus 77.1%, not a same-setting improvement. V2 adds axis-alignment results of 0.40 versus 0.45 and replaces the occlusion-importance findings with gradient-based results. Its Figure 4 and text disagree on some correlations, including ResNet50 neuron values of -0.14 versus 0.09.

T1.justification: The NMF objective is retained, but the mathematical setup replaces logit-drop importance with Gradient×Input and defines average Hoyer axis-alignment. The new selection appendix posits k > s, where s is the unknown number of latent patterns; the MACO optimization formulation disappears. These are limited definitional and assumption changes, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The advantage of dictionary representations and its increase with depth remain central. However, v1's claim that models rely significantly more on distributed features becomes the narrower claim that dictionary elements are no less decision-relevant. V2 adds a major contribution concerning basis-dependent model comparisons, claiming that ResNet50's advantage over VGG16 emerges only with dictionary-based evaluation.

C2.justification: V2 interprets lower axis-alignment as evidence of greater superposition explaining model-comparison outcomes. It adds rationales for NMF and element selection, plus limitations concerning neuron-conditioned dictionaries and evaluation of only two architectures. V1's extended warning that visual coherence need not imply understanding is replaced by an explicit operational definition of interpretability as coherence. The partial-success qualification concerning semantic control remains.

D1.justification: V2 specifies VGG16 layer sampling and clarifies the use of post-ReLU activations. However, it removes v1 Appendices A/B's detailed practice-stimulus and attentiveness-test construction instructions, retaining mainly counts and acceptance thresholds. Core extraction parameters and ImageNet stimulus-pool sizes remain documented.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work around comparative model interpretability and challenges conclusions from neuron-based evaluations. It expands discussion of Zimmermann's automated evaluation work, already represented by a workshop reference in v1, and adds recent SAE literature. It also changes the summary of Zimmermann et al. (2023) from scaling improving interpretability to scaling not improving it.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. Local/distributed terminology becomes neuron-based/dictionary-based, results are reorganized into decision relevance, human performance and model comparison, and the discussion becomes a revised conclusion. The lettered appendices are replaced by a shorter, differently organized appendix.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the principal per-layer bar charts with aggregate comparison bars and depth scatterplots, adds an axis-alignment density plot, and removes the occlusion-importance and mixed-stimulus displays. V1 Figure 3 moves to Figure A1, while Figures 8–10 become A2–A4. Typography, author layout, margins and figure placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 adds valuable replication in a second architecture, clearer terminology and a narrower decision-relevance claim. However, it removes empirical selection-sensitivity and semantic-control evidence and replaces the explicitly specified mixed-effects analysis. Its new depth figure also conflicts numerically with the text. The added comparative evidence and clarity coexist with reduced robustness documentation and reporting inconsistencies, leaving the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
